title: Good News After Anxious Waiting
overview: Paul explains why he sent his helper Timothy to check on the new believers in Thessalonica, shares his relief at the good report, and prays for them.

parts.label: Alone in Athens (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Paul had been forced to leave Thessalonica suddenly and could not get back, so he chose to stay alone in Athens and send Timothy, his close partner, in his place. Timothy's job was to steady and encourage the young group in their trust in Jesus.

parts.label: Trouble was expected (vv. 3-5)
parts.note: Paul reminds them he had warned them that following Jesus would bring hostility, so their hardship was not a sign something had gone wrong. His real fear was that "the tempter," his name for Satan, had used that pressure to pull them away, leaving all his work for nothing.

parts.label: Timothy's good report (vv. 6-8)
parts.note: Timothy came back to Paul, most likely in Corinth, saying they still trusted, still loved, and missed Paul as much as he missed them. Facing troubles of his own, Paul says this news makes him feel truly alive again.

parts.label: Thanks and longing (vv. 9-10)
parts.note: Paul cannot find enough ways to thank God, and he prays constantly to visit and fill in what their faith still lacks. The next chapters hint at what that was: guidance on daily living and questions about believers who had died.

parts.label: A prayer for them (vv. 11-13)
parts.note: He asks God and Jesus to open the way for a visit, and asks that their love grow for each other and for outsiders too. He looks ahead to Jesus' return with all who belong to him, which may mean angels, God's people, or both, and interpreters are not sure which.

think: When someone you care about is far away and going through something hard, what do you find yourself doing with the worry?
